transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got a customer order for 1800 cartons of the new 750-milliliter format that needs to be ready by Monday morning, and Line 6 is available for a Saturday shift. I understand the new format has completed a dry fit on Line 6, but no production run has been authorized yet. That decision is mine to make. Before I can authorize anything, I need to follow our normal Saturday startup routine — I'll need quality, maintenance, and safety to each report and formally record their findings. So let's get started: can I get each of you to walk me through where things stand?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something from my quality review. I completed the review of the new-format trial paperwork yesterday, and it specifies that the first production run requires a 30-minute first-article approval and 100% inspection of the first 200 cartons. The paperwork is still in quality's unfiled trial folder, but the requirement is clear: we'll need to build in time for that first-article approval and full inspection of the first 200 cartons before we can proceed with the rest of the run.

transcript.text: Thanks, Evan. From the maintenance side, I need to flag a critical constraint. I received a firmware record from the vendor this morning for the installed servo controller on Line 6. It confirms that the new 750-milliliter format must run at exactly 90 cartons per minute or slower — no faster. The format changeover also requires a full 2 hours of mechanical setup. I have not yet opened the maintenance work order for the setup, so that needs to happen. Marisol, these are hard constraints that will directly affect our timing and capacity to hit 1800 cartons by Monday morning, and I want to make sure they're on the table before any authorization.

transcript.text: From the safety side, I need to formally report my finding from yesterday's walkdown. The new 750-milliliter format guide adjustment on Line 6 requires two trained employees during setup, and a marked 1.5-meter exclusion zone must be maintained around the infeed. I documented this during the walkdown, but I want to flag that the Saturday startup board has not yet been updated with this finding, so I need to make sure it gets recorded as part of this review.
